title: Industrial Revolution
group: HIST-TOPIC — Overview Anchors (each links to deeper subdomains)
examples: What caused the Industrial Revolution to start in Britain?
How did the factories change people's lives?
What were some of the big changes in society?

explain.say: The Industrial Revolution started because of new inventions. People needed better ways to make things.
Another cause was the growth of trade and resources. More goods meant more money for inventors.
The first big impact was on where people lived. Many moved from farms to crowded cities.
A major impact was on working life. People worked long hours in noisy factories.
Reforms were needed to fix the problems. People started demanding better laws for workers.
In everyday life, think about how we get our clothes. Before, people spun thread by hand at home.

faq.q: Why did the Industrial Revolution start in Britain?
faq.a: Britain had many natural resources like coal and iron. They also had a stable government and growing trade networks.
asks: Why was Britain the starting point?

faq.q: What was the biggest change for workers?
faq.a: Workers moved from working on farms to working in factories. This meant set hours and machine labor.
asks: Did people stop working on farms?

faq.q: What did the reforms actually do?
faq.a: Reforms created laws to limit child labor and set maximum working hours. These laws helped improve safety.
No, while some inventions improved life, the initial working conditions were very harsh for many people.
Yes, the burning of coal for steam power caused much smoke and air pollution in growing cities.

facts: Steam power, often using coal, drove many new machines.
Rapid growth of cities led to overcrowding and poor sanitation.
Early factory workers, including children, often worked very long shifts.
Social reform movements pushed for better factory safety laws.

quiz.say: Moving from rural farms to crowded towns is an example of:
quiz.why: Urbanization describes the rapid growth of cities as people move there for work.

wrong.1: Globalization is about worldwide connection, not just moving to cities.
wrong.2: Migration is the general term for moving, but urbanization is the specific result in cities.
wrong.3: Industrialization is the process of building factories, not the movement of people.

quiz.say: The main goal of early factory reforms was to:

options.show: Move all people to the country
options.say: Move all people to the country

quiz.why: Reforms aimed to protect workers, especially children, from exhausting labor.

wrong.1: The reforms accepted factories but sought to control their harshness.
wrong.2: While wages were an issue, the initial focus of laws was on hours and safety.
wrong.3: It was impossible to reverse the trend of people moving to industrial centers.
